summary: AI observability is essential for understanding how LLM applications behave in production, enabling teams to trace requests, evaluate output quality, track spending, and catch regressions before they impact users. As LLM API costs scale with usage, these tools provide the visibility needed to control spend, debug complex agent workflows, and maintain reliability. Without observability, teams operate blindly on opaque, probabilistic systems that are difficult to debug and expensive to run.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, evaluation scores, and prompt/response quality for LLM and agent applications (especially LangChain-based).
tools.pricing: Free tier limited to ~5,000 monthly traces; paid Plus plans with higher trace limits. 2026 analyses put trace costs at roughly 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that want integrated tracing plus robust evaluation workflows.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request traffic, per-request and aggregate cost, token usage, latency, and caching efficiency via a proxy/gateway.
features: Drop-in proxy gateway with minimal code changes
tools.pricing: Free up to 10,000 requests/traces per month; approximately 79 USD per 100,000 traces on paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-friction cost metering and request monitoring across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Model experiments, training runs, and LLM traces/evaluations (via W&B Weave), including token usage, latency, and output quality.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals and academics; usage-based Team and Enterprise plans with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML teams that need unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the full model lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production ML and LLM performance, including drift, data quality, embedding analysis, evaluations, and tracing (open-source Phoenix).
tools.pricing: Free open-source Phoenix; free tier plus usage-based Pro and custom Enterprise plans for the hosted platform.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade ML/LLM monitoring with drift detection and deep evaluation.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, cost, latency, evaluation scores, and prompt performance for applications and agents.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source for self-hosting; managed cloud with free Hobby tier plus usage-based Pro and Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack with self-hosting flexibility.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and traces using OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation, exportable to any compatible backend.
features: Automatic instrumentation of popular LLM SDKs
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs depend only on the chosen observability backend (e.g., Traceloop, Datadog, Grafana).
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral LLM instrumentation feeding existing observability pipelines.

tools.name: MLflow
tools.monitors: Experiment tracking, model registry, and LLM traces/evaluations, including token usage, latency, and quality metrics.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; hosting costs only, with managed options available via Databricks.
tools.best_for: Teams already using MLflow for ML lifecycle management who want integrated LLM observability.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (via tools like Helicone or prompt caching) to avoid paying for duplicate completions.
Route requests to the cheapest model capable of the task, reserving large frontier models for complex queries only.
Trim prompts and context windows by removing redundant tokens, summarizing history, and using concise system prompts.
Monitor token usage and cost per feature with observability tooling to identify and optimize the most expensive workflows, and set alerts on spending spikes.
